svg.title: Supported unions and restricted relative tensor multiplication
svg.desc: Intrinsic support coreflections identify the actual framed formal union. Equivariant finite Koszul generators give the quotient exterior equivalence. The actual diagonal regular algebra and full module bars identify relative tensor multiplication. Infinite units, differential weights and nonflat intersections distinguish the hypotheses.
svg.text: From intrinsic support to the actual relative tensor functor
Complex curve; connected reductive H; all connective DG bases and unbounded modules.
1. Nested support gives a continuous filtered coreflection — SUL.1–SUL.7
E ⊂ F ⇒ I(F) ⊂ I(E) ⇒ T(E) ⊂ T(F).
Γ(E) = C(E) ⊗ᴸ over B; Γ(E) Γ(F) = Γ(E) = Γ(F) Γ(E).
T = Loc{K(E)}; C(S) = colim C(E); Γ(S) = C(S) ⊗ᴸ over B.
K(E) is compact; the supported tensor unit C(S) need not be compact.
Every comparison is the factorization of the original coreflection counit.
2. The full formal union has explicit inverse functors — SUL.8–SUL.12
supported M
system (M(E))
U: M ↦ (Γ(E)M)
V: (M(E)) ↦ colim M(E)
Γ(E) colim M(F) ≃ M(E) on the cofinal tail F ⊃ E; VU = Γ(S) = identity.
External compact Koszul generators also identify QCoh(Y) ⊗ QCoh(Y) ≃ QCoh(Y²).
3. Equivariance includes the differential and all higher action maps — SUL.13–SUL.19
Choose a finite H-stable W(E) ⊂ I(E) generating the ordinary ideal.
Exact rational invariants lift W(E) → H⁰(B) to W(E) → B.
P(E) = Sym(W(E)) → B; Kᴴ(E) = B ⊗ᴸ over P(E) with C.
The full pushout bar lies in QCoh(BH); its Koszul differential is H-equivariant.
P(E,V) = Kᴴ(E) ⊗ V, for finite H-representations V, compactly generate A.
4. Exterior Hom tests identify the quotient product and dual — SUL.20–SUL.26
Two finite perfect Koszul duals and two Reynolds projections give
Hom(P ⊠ Q, P′ ⊠ Q′) ≃ Hom(P,P′) ⊗ Hom(Q,Q′).
Full module bars: A ⊗ A ≃ QCoh(Z²); A∨ = modules over the opposite DG category.
m(A): diagonal pullback after ext. δ(A): inverse ext after diagonal pushforward.
The actual affine diagonal identifies (L ⊗ L)(Rᵣ) ≃ δ(A)(1).
5. The regular algebra proves the actual relative multiplication — SUL.27–SUL.30
Compact dualizable Ran generators make δ(R) continuous and bimodule-linear.
Tests from 1 ⊠ X make δ(R) conservative; its full free bars give R ≃ Mod(Rᵣ).
A ⊗ over R with A ≃ Mod((L ⊗ L)(Rᵣ), A ⊗ A) ≃ A.
On free objects this functor sends a ⊠ b to a ⊗ b; action maps and full bars agree.
No compact-unit assumption on A enters this coefficient-change argument.
6. Exact examples distinguish the necessary assertions — SUL.31–SUL.42
All closed points of a line: H¹(C(S)) = C(t)/C[t] = sum of all principal parts.
Its infinitely many primary components make the supported unit noncompact.
x of weight 1: dη = x forces weight(η) = 1; all representation twists are needed.
C ⊗ᴸ over C[t,u] with C = Λ(εₜ,εᵤ): degrees 0, −1, −2 have dimensions 1,2,1.
Elliptic Gₘ: infinitely many root-pair components make 1(A) noncompact.
The right adjoint of L is then not continuous, while relative multiplication is ≃.
Exact proofs: §§3.167–3.179, SUL.1–SUL.42; Solutions3.DA–3.DD.
Relative tensor framework: AGKRRV, arXiv:2010.01906v2.
